unit.name: ratchet
unit.rows: none: no compiled engine code changes
unit.more: and then the new lists group by its name ("sh scripts/check.sh <its name>") and the cost group's red input alone ("sh scripts/cost-red.sh" as the cost group runs it; the builder ran the whole cost group once through the new base path and its log is in the change's directory: read its EXIT line, do not run the whole group again)
unit.brief:
THE OWNER'S DECISION (20 Nov, verbatim): "Yeah, I think I agree on using CI for enforcing invariants. Let's just make sure that the CI checks use the same job that we run locally, e.g. make test." It answers a question about .github/CODEOWNERS, which unit G1-1 added to hold tests/data/couplings.txt to 'only goes down' across changes (the wall test in tests/source.rs sees one tree and cannot). The decision: a list's 'only goes down' is held by a check, not by CODEOWNERS, and that check, like every check CI makes, is run by the same command locally and in CI. In this repository that command is sh scripts/check.sh <group> (read its header and CLAUDE.md's 'Running the checks': every gate this repository has broken broke as a check that was not running or a verdict not earned, and 'a second definition of the checks is how the next one starts').

WHAT THE TREE HAS (verify each; the tree is right where this differs): .github/CODEOWNERS with one line for tests/data/couplings.txt; the lists tests/data/couplings.txt (tab-separated: file, scope, token, region, count, stage, reason; the wall test compares totals by file, token and region), tests/data/door.txt and tests/data/door-libc.txt (the door's exemptions, G1-2), tests/data/cost-entries.txt (G1-3: each public entry point held to a probe that counts it or to a reason why none does); .github/workflows/ci.yml whose jobs call sh scripts/check.sh <groups> except two departures: the cross-arm job runs cargo itself with a linker, a qemu runner and a --cfg in the YAML's env (scripts/check.sh's header says 'Not here, deliberately: cross-arm ... CI-only'), and the cost job computes its base in YAML shell (PR base, else the push's before, else HEAD~1) before calling sh scripts/check.sh cost with COST_BASE.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(1) scripts/base.sh: the one definition of 'the commit a change is made on', printed as a full sha. An explicit override first, then a pull request's base, then a push's before (not when empty or all zeros), then the merge-base of HEAD with origin/main; CI passes only event values in the environment and base.sh does the deciding. A base that cannot be resolved to a commit in this clone (a shallow clone, no origin/main, a sha that is not there) is a failure with a message that says what to do, never a pass and never a silent fallback. The cost group takes its base from it (COST_BASE stays as the explicit override for that group; keep what the cost job does today for a branch's first push, decided in base.sh and stated). Its red inputs: each unresolvable case exits nonzero.
(2) The lists' check and its red input (scripts/ratchet.sh and scripts/ratchet-red.sh, or better names; a helper in python beside them is fine, as scripts/cost-diff.py is): for each REGISTERED list, compare the list at merge-base(HEAD, base) with the list in the tree and fail on growth. Growth is defined a list at a time by what the list is for, in one registry that names each list, how a line's key and its number are read, and one line of why (couplings.txt: a total by file, token and region that is higher, or a key that is new; the door's two lists and cost-entries.txt's reasons-in-place-of-a-probe: read each file and its test and decide what a new exemption is there). A registered list that the base had and the tree lacks fails; a list new since the base has nothing to hold yet and says so; a list file under tests/data that looks like a ratchet (decide the rule and state it) and is not registered fails, so the next list cannot be added without registering. An intended raise is declared in the change, in a file of its own (list, key, from, to, reason), and passes only if it matches what the check observed exactly; a declaration that matches nothing observed and is not already in the base (spent) fails; say what a spent declaration is and when it is removed, and make sure a change after a merged raise is not red for it. The verdict prints every raise it let through, so a reader of the log sees what was raised. The red input runs the check on scratch copies or fixtures, each case by its exit status: growth undeclared (red), growth declared exactly (green, printed), declared with a wrong number (red), a declaration for nothing (red), a list removed (red), an unregistered list (red), a count lowered (green), an unresolvable base (red), the tree against itself (green).
(3) scripts/check.sh: a group for the lists' check (it runs the red input and then the check, as the cost group does), in the default set unless you find a factual reason against (say it); a cross-arm group outside the default set that carries what the YAML's env carries today (the YAML keeps only installing the toolchain and the group's call); the header's 'Not here, deliberately' paragraph and its 'CI calls the same groups' sentence made true.
(4) .github/workflows/ci.yml: a job for the lists group (fetch-depth 0); cross-arm through check.sh; the cost job's base logic gone from the YAML (event values in env, base.sh decides). Every job's checking is sh scripts/check.sh <group>.
(5) tests/source.rs: a test that reads .github/workflows/ci.yml and fails a run step that checks anything other than through sh scripts/check.sh (set-up commands on a short allow list in the test, each with why it is set-up; a cargo, a python or a script of scripts/ called from the YAML to check something is red; shell that decides a base or a verdict in the YAML is red), and fails a group scripts/check.sh knows that no CI job runs unless a line says why. Its red inputs are edits of the YAML's text in the test, as the other source tests edit sources.
(6) Remove .github/CODEOWNERS.
(7) Docs: scripts/check.sh's header; CLAUDE.md's 'Running the checks' (the groups it names; add a rule only if the work taught one, with the failure that taught it, in that file's manner); README.md only if it lists groups or CI. Nothing under scratch/ (the launcher files the notes).

WHAT NOT TO BUILD: nothing for the cost gate's moves between functions (a later change may use a declaration of the same kind for a group of functions held to its net: shape the declaration's file so that would not need a second mechanism, and stop there); no change to any list's content, to the wall, door or cost tests' own rules, or to anything under src/.

SHOW: the lists group red on its red input and green on the tree, by exit status; the lists group green against the real base of this branch (merge-base with origin/main after 'git fetch origin main') with every raise it reports explained (the lists were all added on this branch, so each is 'new since the base': if the check has nothing to hold today, prove it holds by the red input and by a run against a base on this branch where a list existed, e.g. the commit before G1-3's); sh scripts/check.sh cost run once whole through the new base path against the commit before (a self-check that reads green; it builds the suite's probes twice and takes most of an hour and several gigabytes: read df first, one cargo at a time, in the background with its EXIT line), its log kept in the change's directory with the base it resolved; the cross-arm group's command line shown equal to what the YAML ran (it cannot run here without the cross toolchain and qemu: if scripts/deps.sh or apt can install them in this container, run it, else say it is unverified here and show the env it exports). Mutants: at least eight of your own across base.sh, the check, the registry and the YAML test (a base that falls back silently, growth read by line count in place of the key, a declaration matched loosely, the unregistered-list rule dropped, a group nobody runs let through, an allow-listed command that hides a check).
